text: Give an LDraw LEGO© model to an AI agent, get back a Blender-animated version of it. The agent will: Note The installation process will install every required tool and dependency locally on this project repo, in order to avoid polluting the host OS . However, there is a requirement of setting several env vars on rc files, like e.g. .bashrc or .zshrc The installed dependencies, like e.g. Blender, are git-ignored by default. You'll need Python 3.12+ installed. Start by cloning the repo and running the setup script , pick the right one for your OS: git clone https://github.com/anteloc/ldraw-mecha.git cd ldraw-mecha ./setup-macos.sh # or ./setup-linux.sh, ./setup-win-wsl.sh Installed during setup Item Version uv 0.9.3 bun 1.4.4 ldraw-annotator 0.5.0 ldraw-xray 0.5.0 jev-rerank 0.5.0 mpd2glb 0.9.1 Blender 5.2.3 LeoCAD 26.09 LDraw parts library latest At the end of the setup process, you'll get a snippet with the env vars to be added to your shell profile ( .bashrc , .zshrc , etc.), something like e.g.: # >>> ldraw-mecha (from setup-macos.sh) >>> export LDRAW_DIR= " /Users/me/ldraw-mecha/data/ldraw " export LDRAWDIR= " $LDRAW_DIR " export BLENDER_BIN= " /Users/me/ldraw-mecha/bin/Blender.app/Contents/MacOS/Blender " export LEOCAD= " /Users/me/ldraw-mecha/bin/LeoCAD.app/Contents/MacOS/LeoCAD " export LDRAW_XRAY_CACHE= " /Users/me/ldraw-mecha/.cache/ldraw-xray " export LDRAW_ANNOTATOR_DB= " /Users/me/ldraw-mecha/data/ldraw-info.db " # export TYPESAFE_API_KEY=... # optional: Jev semantic search (jev-rerank) # other env vars... # <<< ldraw-mecha <<< If you're on VS Code or a terminal , restart it in order to get an updated env with the newly added env vars. For inspecting and selecting one pre-annotated model to animate, open the annotated models selector by running: python3 model-selector/serve.py Then, take a look at the Process guide for a step-by-step usage example . Note More samples available at: Gallery Animations have been generated from original models , not from ai-generated ones. These are some samples of animations by different agents, take a look at their Summaries for more details. ▶ Video · Summary Original ▶ Video · Summary ▶ Video · Summary After publishing LDraw Nova , a sibling project for agentic generation of LDraw models , several people reached out to me asking about if models could be animated somehow. During the development of Nova, I noticed that adding some special annotations to .mpd original model source files , and then giving those to agents , would: Which gave me the idea that, maybe, an agent would also understand how a model would work. As a first step to it, I gave annotated models to different agents, and prompted them to infer (reverse-engineer) their constituent submodels (see Haiku 5.5. experiment below). Results from inference experiments were both pretty good and consistent across different agents, and I also noticed the following: many of the submodels inferred were actually mechanisms. After questioning several agents about those inferred mechanisms, regarding how would they actually work , I also got consistent results: agents would describe behaviours based on the descriptions for the parts on a mechanism! 🤯 At this point, I had the following: The result of an actual divide-and-conquer process , right? 🤓 Which would make handling individual mechanisms manageable. 🤩 Now, there was the matter of giving agents the means to actually animate mechanisms they already knew how they worked. I was playing with Blender MCP at the time, and Blender looked promising as a tool that would provide agents a way to manipulate LDraw models in 3D , imported into Blender as glTF (.glb) files. But there was still an open issue: How to map from a refined model source code an agent would understand, to its equivalent 3D model in glTF format an agent could manipulate? And the solution I found was: Annotate the 3D glTF model's nodes with the same annotations as the source code, so the agent would: Now, I had a draft for a process , but no tools for the agent to use and carry it forward. Given that the process would require a high amount of complex geometric and spatial calculations , I asked the agent to derive a new python toolset from the one created for ldraw-nova The new python toolset I refined iteratively , by giving the agent simple models at the beginning, and increasingly complex ones each time. And to test it, I gave an agent instructions to: And it finally worked ! 🚀🚀🚀 (but not perfectly) 😜 Prompt: This is a fragment, a submodel, from an LDraw .mpd file model. It sits on a 2x12 dark-grey base plate, with a grille tile at the -X end and two light-grey inverted tiles at the +X end. The ridge slope carries red "NASA" and black "ESA" printing, so it likely comes from a space-agency-themed LEGO model, though the parts alone don't identify the exact set. The split below follows the physical groups, which also match the three build steps in the original. The parent comes first, then its children ( hull-shell.ldr and end-cap-tiles.ldr ), then the grandchildren (the two slope rows).
